extracted.intended_audience: editors/compilers of posthumous conversational collections; literary readers and scholars interested in Coleridge's table talk
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for collecting, selecting, and presenting a deceased author's conversational remarks ('table talk') from memory or notes, with attention to fidelity of manner, selection criteria, and editorial annotation. Applies to producing a published volume of remembered conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record principal topics in speaker's own words
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to writing the principal topics of his conversation in his own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor notes that on first visiting he 'committed to writing, as well as I could, the principal topics of his conversation in his own words.' Emphasis on attempting literal reproduction of the speaker's phrasing where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select only parts fit for present publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only such parts as seem fit for present publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor explicitly restricts the volume to items judged publishable now, implying a selection filter based on taste, relevance, and propriety rather than publishing everything recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid naming living persons except by common literary/political notoriety
rubrics_metrics.description: No living person's name is introduced, whether for praise or for blame, except on literary or political grounds of common notoriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule aims to avoid gratuitous identification of private individuals and to limit references to public figures whose mention is already common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer exposition over dialogue reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attempt to give dialogue—condense recollections into intelligible wholes rather than staged dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor states there was seldom much dialogue to give and that his practice was to condense what he could remember on each topic into paragraphs (wholes) to preserve precision and sense rather than attempt verbatim conversational turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condense recollections into intelligible wholes with minimal injury to manner and diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Condense recollections into intelligible wholes with as little injury to the living manner and diction as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When memory fragments conversation, the editor's method is to form coherent paragraphs that keep the speaker's tone and characteristic expressions intact, balancing clarity and fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reflection to recover order and characteristic expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recover order and characteristic expressions by thinking the argument over again; order and expressions will spontaneously arise with practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, subtle discourse is hard to recall; the editor recommends reworking the remembered argument mentally to restore sequence and phrasing with reasonable accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and accept fragmentary nature of specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens will be fragmentary and therefore deficient in one of the most distinguishing properties of that which they are designed to represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compiler should be candid about limitations: fragments cannot fully reproduce continuous conversational flow; grouping into separate paragraphs is a trade-off for precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add notes and quotations from the speaker's works for elucidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a few notes, and make some quotations from the speaker's own works for the purpose of general elucidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editorial notes and internal quotations to clarify references, link conversational remarks to published works, and help readers examine the principles the speaker relied on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid editorial commentary on justice of speaker's remarks; let principles speak
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid extensive commentary on the justice of the remarks; the principles upon which the speaker founded his observations are generally expressly stated and may be examined by themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor disclaims heavy critical commentary, preferring to present the speaker's stated principles and allow readers to judge, intervening only for elucidation where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include controversial or 'illiberal' opinions if they were deliberately entertained
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not omit passages merely because they may be pronounced illiberal; include opinions deliberately entertained by the speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor defends including potentially offensive views when they accurately reflect the speaker's deliberate positions, rather than excluding them out of deference or fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize preserving the speaker's living manner and musical utterance
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to preserve the living manner, diction, and the 'tones' of the speaker's discourse, since oral delivery may convey subtleties not easily captured on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, retain cadence, simplicity of language, musical tone, and the distinctive transitions and links that characterize the speaker's oral style; acknowledge some subtleties may be irrecoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about editorial responsibility and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the responsibility incurred by publication and explain editorial methods and limitations in a preface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor explicitly sets out his motives, methods (note-taking, selection), limitations (memory, fragmentation), and willingness to 'abide the result,' which helps readers assess editorial reliability.
